definition: Apple Numbers is a spreadsheet application for working with tables, formulas, and charts on Apple platforms.
example: A household builds a monthly spending sheet with a chart that updates as entries change.

definition: appletviewer was a Java development tool for running and testing Java applets without opening a browser.
example: A maintainer tests an archived applet in an isolated legacy Java environment.

definition: An application delivery controller manages network traffic to applications and commonly provides load balancing, health checks, and protocol termination.
example: A controller stops routing requests to an application server that fails its health checks.

definition: Application monitoring collects signals about software performance, availability, and errors to detect and investigate failures.
example: An operator traces rising response times to one slow database call.

definition: The applied element method represents a structure as elements connected by springs to model deformation, separation, and collapse.
example: An engineer uses the method to examine how a damaged frame redistributes loads.

definition: Applixware was an office suite for Unix-like systems that included document, spreadsheet, and presentation tools.
example: An archivist opens an old Applixware spreadsheet in a compatible environment to recover its data.

definition: AppsFlyer is a marketing measurement platform that relates app installations and events to acquisition campaigns.
example: A marketing team compares the reported installs attributed to two ad campaigns.

definition: AppSheet is a low-code platform for building applications and automations over existing data sources.
example: A maintenance team turns a spreadsheet of inspection records into a mobile form.

definition: Apptio provides business-management software for analyzing technology costs and relating spending to services and organizational units.
example: A finance partner allocates cloud spending across product teams for review.

definition: apxs is an Apache HTTP Server tool for compiling and installing extension modules as shared objects.
example: A server maintainer rebuilds an existing module for a compatible Apache installation.

definition: Arachnophilia is a text-based web authoring editor with tools for writing and editing HTML.
example: A site maintainer updates hand-written markup in an archived page.

definition: ArangoDB is a multi-model database that supports documents, key-value access, and graphs in one system.
example: A service stores customer profiles as documents and queries links between related accounts.

definition: Araxis Merge is a visual tool for comparing and merging files or directory trees.
example: A developer reconciles conflicting edits to a configuration file.

definition: Architectural rendering creates a visual depiction of a building or space from drawings or a digital model.
example: A designer produces a view showing how an interior would look in afternoon light.

definition: Architectural visualization communicates built-environment designs through representations such as images, diagrams, walkthroughs, or interactive models.
example: A design team uses a walkthrough to help clients understand movement through a proposed library.
sense_note: This broader practice includes rendering rather than being identical to it.

definition: ArcSight Enterprise Security Manager collects and correlates security events to support monitoring and incident investigation.
example: A security analyst reviews correlated authentication events across several approved systems.

definition: Areca Backup is a file backup tool that manages backup sets and restoration across supported storage destinations.
example: A user restores an older version of an accidentally overwritten project file.

definition: Argo CD is a GitOps delivery tool that compares Kubernetes deployments with declared configuration and synchronizes differences.
example: A team reviews a configuration change in Git before Argo CD applies it to a cluster.

definition: ARKit is Apple’s framework for integrating digitally rendered objects with a device’s view of the physical world.
example: A furniture app anchors a virtual table to a floor visible through the camera.

definition: The Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application was an electronic health record system for U.S. military healthcare.
example: A clinician reviews an eligible patient’s documented outpatient visits across military facilities.

definition: Arquillian is a Java testing framework that runs integration tests within or against application containers.
example: A developer tests whether a dependency-injected service behaves correctly in its container.

definition: Arranging catering coordinates food service, menu requirements, logistics, and timing for an event.
example: An organizer confirms dietary needs and delivery times with a caterer before a workshop.

definition: Arranging conferences coordinates venues, schedules, speakers, participants, and event operations.
example: An organizer prepares an accessible venue and resolves timetable conflicts between sessions.

definition: ArtStation is an online portfolio and community platform for visual artists working in fields such as games, film, and illustration.
example: A character artist publishes a portfolio piece with supporting design sketches and model views.

definition: As-built drawings document the locations and details of work as actually constructed rather than only as originally planned.
example: A facilities team checks an as-built drawing before opening a wall to locate an installed conduit.

definition: Ashampoo Burning Studio is software for creating, copying, and managing supported optical discs.
example: A user writes a verified set of archived photos to a disc supported by the drive.

definition: ASP.NET Core MVC is a .NET web framework for organizing application logic into models, views, and controllers.
example: A controller retrieves product data and passes it to a view that renders a product page.

definition: ASP.NET Identity is a Microsoft framework for adding user accounts, authentication, and related identity features to ASP.NET applications.
example: A developer integrates password reset and role-based access into a web application.
sense_note: Clarify whether the historical ASP.NET or ASP.NET Core identity implementation is required.

definition: ASP.NET Web API is a .NET framework for building HTTP services, especially APIs accessed by clients beyond web browsers.
example: A developer exposes product inventory through an endpoint used by a mobile application.
sense_note: The label can refer specifically to the earlier framework rather than ASP.NET Core web APIs.

definition: An asphalt batch mix plant produces asphalt in discrete batches by weighing and mixing heated aggregates and binder.
example: An operator checks that a production batch matches the specified mixture.

definition: An assembly drawing shows how components fit together in a product or system and may identify parts or their relationships.
example: A technician uses an exploded assembly view to locate a spacer among several fasteners.

definition: Assessing patient needs gathers and interprets information about a patient’s health, functioning, preferences, and support requirements.
example: A care team documents mobility limitations before planning discharge support.

definition: Asthma education helps patients and caregivers understand asthma, recognize warning signs, and follow a clinician-approved management plan.
example: An educator checks that a patient can explain when to follow their written action plan.

definition: Async and await are language constructs that express asynchronous operations in a sequential-looking form without necessarily blocking the executing thread.
example: A client application waits for a server response while allowing its interface to remain responsive.

definition: Atlassian Confluence is a collaboration platform for creating and organizing shared pages, documentation, and project knowledge.
example: A team documents design decisions on a shared page and maintains its revision history.

definition: Atlassian Crucible is a tool for collaborative code review and discussion of changes.
example: Reviewers annotate specific lines and track issues before accepting a change.

definition: Atomic layer deposition deposits thin films through repeated, self-limiting surface reactions.
example: A fabrication team uses the process to specify a uniform film thickness over a patterned surface.

definition: AtScale provides a semantic layer that lets analytics tools use shared business metrics over underlying data platforms.
example: A company defines revenue once and uses the definition across multiple dashboards.

definition: auditd is a Linux userspace daemon that records events supplied by the Linux Audit subsystem.
example: An administrator reviews records of changes to a monitored configuration file.

definition: Auditing inpatient coding checks that diagnoses and procedures recorded for admitted patients are consistently supported by clinical documentation and applicable coding rules.
example: An auditor compares an assigned procedure code with the operative report and records any discrepancy.
